item.title: Python String Formatting: How to Print a Literal Percent Sign Amidst Placeholders
item.description:
“Python String Formatting: How to Print a Literal Percent Sign Amidst Placeholders”

When manipulating strings in Python using standard formatting techniques—be it the classic modulo operator (%), the .format() method, or modern f-strings—the percent sign (%) carries a special significance as a placeholder introducer. A frequent requirement arises when one needs to embed a literal percent character within the string while simultaneously substituting variables using format specifiers (e.g., %s, %d). How does one instruct Python to display the % character plainly without treating it as the start of a substitution directive?

item.title: Python String Literals Escaping Backslashes: Practical Solutions Explained
item.description:
“Python String Literals Escaping Backslashes: Practical Solutions Explained”

When working with Python strings, the backslash character (\) holds a special significance as an escape character. This means it can alter the interpretation of the character immediately following it, enabling representations like newlines (\n) or tabs (\t). However, this special role presents a challenge when you intend to print a literal backslash itself. How do you display a backslash character without Python interpreting it as an escape sequence?
